title: Modernize batch prioritization and KV lease reconciliation
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Problem:
The continuous batching subsystem exhibits unstable latency spikes under mixed-priority traffic. High-priority interactive requests are sometimes delayed behind large background inference batches due to coarse lane assignment and an all-or-nothing prefetch strategy. Separately, the KV lease subsystem experiences transient conflicts during shard rebalance and autoscaling events: leases bounce between hosts leading to degraded KV hit rates and increased cold starts.

Goal:
1) Introduce a priority-aware batching layer with a priority gradient (soft reservations) to guarantee p99 for latency-sensitive lanes while preserving throughput for background work.
2) Replace current lease handoff with a reconciliation protocol that reduces flip-flopping by introducing "soft-sticky" leases and a monotonic handover grace period.
3) Make these changes rollable behind feature flags with metrics and failure-mode fallbacks.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- p99 latency for interactive lane improves by >= 20% under mixed traffic in the canary cluster (measured with synthetic mix).
- Average KV hit rate recovers to within 2% of baseline after a shard rebalance event.
- No increased tail errors (5xx) during 5% canary rollout.
- Implementation covered by unit + integration tests and end-to-end benchmark harness.

Proposed design (high level):
- Batching: introduce BatchPriorityV2 that assigns each request a floating priority score (0..1). Scheduler maintains a priority gradient across N lanes (hot, warm, cold) but allows dynamic promotion/demotion of batches based on observed latency and queue age. Add prefetch window tuning: smaller prefetch for hot lane, speculative prefetch for warm lane.
- Lease reconciliation: add LeaseHeader v2 to KV metadata, include last-holder timestamp and epoch. Implement a reconcile loop that waits a grace window before force-takeover; if two hosts contest a lease, use deterministic tie-breaker (host-id + epoch) and emit a lease_conflict metric.
- Rollout: behind flags batch_priority_v2 and lease_reconcile_v2. Start in internal canary with 5% traffic and 2-hour observation. Provide automatic rollback on p99 breach or lease_conflicts_per_min > threshold.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Spike: prototype priority gradient in a branch with synthetic driver (3 days).
2) Core impl: add BatchPriorityV2, prefetch tuning knobs, and LeaseHeader v2 (10 days).
3) Tests & Harness: integration test for simulated rebalance and mixed traffic (4 days).
4) Observability: add metrics (batch_size_avg, batch_wait_ms_p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, lease_conflicts_per_min, lease_handover_time) and dashboard (2 days).
5) Canary rollout and follow-up fixes (5 days).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: priority gradient reduces overall throughput. Mitigation: monitor tokens/sec and expose config knobs to tune lane weights; revert flag if throughput drops >5%.
- Risk: new lease protocol introduces availability gaps during migration. Mitigation: dual-write compatibility for LeaseHeader v1+v2 and gradual switch-over with feature flag.

Dependencies:
- ENG-4723 (batch scheduler consolidation) — will unblock integration with new scheduler hooks.
- ENG-30712 (slot allocator observability) — helps correlate slot pressure with batching decisions.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal drive): https://drive.redwood.company/docs/serving/batch-priority-v2-design
- Benchmark harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/274
- Spike notes (notebook): https://notebooks.redwood.company/spikes/batch-priority-v2

Release target: runtime-1.20
Security review required: false
Customer impact: medium

Notes:
- Prior work references: existing continuous batching code is fragile around lane promotion; see ENG-8240 and ENG-15903 for historical context but this implementation focuses on graceful degradation rather than immediate eviction-based policies.
